title: Bijectivity of canonical homology evaluation
statement: Let k be any commutative ring and choose the derived category of ModuleCat k [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. For every derived object A and every integer n, the explicitly constructed k-linear map cupHomologyEvaluation [def-sc-module-cup-homology-evaluation] from Hom(Q(S(n)),A) to H^n(A) is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 13.19.8, followed by evaluation of a single-complex chain map and its homotopy on 1

proof.text: The single free rank-one complex is bounded above and degreewise projective, hence K-projective. For A=Q(K), identify derived morphisms from Q(S(n)) with chain maps modulo homotopy by the bounded-projective localization bijection.

A map from S(n) is determined by the image of 1, which is a cycle. For two maps, a chain homotopy exists exactly when their cycles differ by a boundary: its only possible nonzero component sends 1 into degree n-1, and its differential is that boundary. Thus homotopy classes are bijective with degree-n homology classes. Naturality of homologyFunctorFactors and the single-complex generator formula identify this bijection with the specified evaluation map.

Every derived object is isomorphic to Q(K). Postcomposition with the isomorphism and applying homology are bijections. Functoriality intertwines evaluation with these maps, transferring bijectivity to A.
